name: Mid-century
summary: A 1950s flat-colour how-to card: fills printed a few pixels off a broken, breathing ink line, one colour plane per scene with a floor band, a held presenter whose hand does the step, slab titles on off-register plates, numbered medallions, atomic sparkles and starbursts.

palette.use: paper: the ground, caption cards, drop shadows
paper shade: drop shadows, second plates
warm black: all lines and slab lettering
coral dark: the shade inside coral shapes
coral: the presenter's sweater, caption stars
turquoise, the subject: blue light keeps this one colour all film

type.case: sentence for slab titles; letter-spaced caps for small labels
type.emphasis: the numbered medallion and data landing on the picture on the action beat

banned: 1930s rubber hose: no black-and-white, no bouncing world, no hot jazz
a whiteboard explainer: pictures are printed, not written on
anything pure or neon; gradients; a handheld camera; dissolves
data as a slide: data lands on the picture on the action beat
the subject on its own colour, or the presenter on their own accent
stretched standing arms; a separate nose wedge; fat-blob fingers; zoomed-world close-ups
copying any 1950s studio's or designer's characters, drawings, lettering or music, or naming them
